title: Two Seymour vertices in every sink-free oriented graph
abstract_plain_text: We prove, relative to two explicitly stated results of the pinned OpenAI manuscript on Seymour's conjecture, that every nonempty finite sink-free oriented graph has two distinct vertices whose exact second out-neighborhood is at least as large as their first. This is Conjecture 2 of Dara, Francis, Jacob and Narayanan. The inputs are the ordinary one-vertex Seymour theorem and a finite-relation pruning lemma; their truth is stipulated here. A minimum counterexample has a unique good vertex with one successor. Deleting that vertex leaves weak subset deficits together with a strict inequality for subsets that do not reach the successor in one or two steps. In a transitive blowup, compatibility with the diagonal selects many fibers with this strict inequality. Their total gain dominates the possible losses of all remaining fibers, allowing the established pruning objective to close. All deductions from the two inputs are proved below. Finite diagnostics and formal supporting lemmas are distinguished from the full graph theorem.
comments: This is an AI-assisted preprint with internal independent agent reviews, not external peer review. The two stated OpenAI/math inputs at revision fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb are stipulated premises. The contribution comparison is bounded. Eleven Lean supporting theorems certify boundary, aggregation and conditional cardinality/pruning implications; the full graph theorem is not formalized.
